newsitem.title: USA: Brent sinks in late US trade, foreign crudes ample.
newsitem.headline: Brent sinks in late US trade, foreign crudes ample.

text.p: North Sea Brent sank for the second consecutive day in late U.S. trading Thursday amid heavy selling by a major Wall Street player, traders said.
A series of partial paper Brents for March changed hands in the aftermarket at $22.90/22.91/22.95 a barrel, down 12-17 cents from the IPE settlement of $23.07.
February/March spreads traded at 28/30/31 cents, steady to slightly lower from a late-day range of 30-33 cents, traders said.
Meanwhile, the U.S. Gulf Coast continues to feature a bevy of foreign crudes, thanks to a widening transatlantic arbitrage, traders and refiners said.
The spread between West Texas Intermediate and Brent moved out 10-20 cents to around $2.00 a barrel, brightening the economics of transatlantic trade.
A U.S. company is offering Brent for end February-early March arrival at March WTI minus 35-40 cents a barrel, while a Wall Streeter is working a VLCC of Brent for early February loading.
Another Wall Street firm is showing West African Forcados and Bonny Light for arrival the first decade of March at March WTI plus 40 and 30 cents, respectively.
Latin American sweet crudes, like U.S. domestics, have been pummeled by the onslaught of North Sea and West African barrels.

Colombia's state-owned Ecopetrol sold a cargo of Cusiana for February 12-16 to a Gulf Coast refiner at a 50-60 cent discount to March WTI, down from a pre-Christmas premium of around 40 cents, traders said.
Elsewhere in Colombia, a European equity producer has pushed forward the dates on a Vasconia cargo to January 27-28 from January 19-20, in a renewed effort to sell.
Traders thought the cargo would eventually get placed around $2.50 under WTI.
